package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affected Mac and Windows versions distributed prior to March 30th, 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CX Desktop App was compromised via a software supply chain attack, resulting in the distribution of malicious code within trusted application binaries. The attackers inserted malware into the app, which was then delivered to end users through official update channels, enabling targeted information theft.

execution_context.file_location: Electron app resource files (e.g., disguised as icon files from a GitHub repository)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious payload embedded in files named as icons, downloaded from a GitHub repository named 'IconStorages'. The files appear benign but contain executable malware.
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely shellcode or binary payload, possibly loaded via JavaScript in Electron)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the application loads files from a remote GitHub repository, interprets them as icons, but actually executes embedded malicious code, enabling information theft and further payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and executing code from files disguised as icons, especially from a public GitHub repository, is highly abnormal and indicative of an attempt to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Electron apps may load static assets (icons, images) from trusted sources, but should never execute code from such files or fetch executable content from untrusted remote repositories.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may update icons or assets from a CDN, but would not execute code from these files.
key_indicators: Fetching files from a GitHub repository at runtime
Files named as icons containing executable payloads
Execution of code from non-executable file formats

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the 3CX Desktop App build process, embedding logic to fetch and execute payloads from a remote repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious payload on end-user systems

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the compromised app fetches files from a GitHub repository ('IconStorages'), treating them as icons but actually executing embedded malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware execution and potential information theft

attack_chain.action: Malware targets specific users (e.g., cryptocurrency companies) for information theft, leveraging the trusted 3CX app as a delivery mechanism.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure

behavioral_signatures: Electron apps fetching and executing code from remote repositories at runtime
Loading files with benign extensions (e.g., .ico, .png) and executing their contents
Unexpected network requests to public GitHub repositories from production applications
file_indicators: Files named as icons (e.g., *.ico, *.png) containing executable payloads
References to 'IconStorages' or similar suspicious repositories in application code or logs
network_indicators: Connections to github.com/IconStorages or similar repositories at runtime
Unexpected outbound connections from Electron apps to public code hosting platforms
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Electron-based applications for runtime network requests to public repositories, especially those fetching files with benign extensions. Analyze fetched files for embedded executable content. Flag any code execution originating from non-executable file types or from files downloaded at runtime. Review application update and asset-fetching logic for deviations from expected behavior.
